1#HN:# Suite Framework: Solstice Soul Personality Suite
  2#KM:
  3#HV:> Status: v0.3 framework document. Suite template and methodology locked. Tests 1 and 2 complete. Tests 3 and 4 in proposal. Construct-anchor citations for Tests 3 and 4 reviewed for relevance.
  4#MP:> Purpose: define the overall design before Tests 3 and 4 are built, so the four tests measure different aspects of personality with minimal overlap.
  5#NQ:> Scope: themes, domains, test names, result types, and the same-versus-different decision for methodology and theory.
  6#SY:
  7#RR:---
  8#XW:
  9#SZ:## 1. The design principle: one theme, one personality domain
 10#SK:
 11#VT:Each theme maps to one recognized sub-discipline of personality psychology. The four tests together answer four different self-knowledge questions. No two tests measure the same thing.
 12#TX:
 13#SB:| Theme | Domain | Self-knowledge question |
 14#YB:|---|---|---|
 15#XV:| Solstice | Affect, energy, motivation | How do you burn? |
 16#RP:| Turing | Cognition | How do you compute? |
 17#TQ:| Pride | Identity, self-concept, self-expression | How do you show who you are? |
 18#QX:| Passage of Time | Temporality | How do you move through time? |
 19#YT:
 20#QX:This partition is the suite's main strength. Affect, cognition, identity, and time are four established research areas, each with its own validated instruments. The final synthesis combines four genuinely additive signals into one self-portrait.
 21#RJ:
 22#QW:---
 23#NV:
 24#ZB:## 2. Same methodology, different theory
 25#XW:
 26#JS:**Methodology is the same across all four tests.** Locked. Non-negotiable. This is the facet-level structural model used by serious instruments (NEO-PI-R organizes its domains into facets). It is the most advanced structure achievable through design and literature synthesis alone.
 27#JJ:
 28#RR:**Response format.**
 29#JZ:- Seven-point bipolar Likert (segmented pips between two anchor statements).
 30#VP:- Pole direction randomized per item to counter position bias; the bipolar two-anchor format counters acquiescence bias.
 31#SZ:
 32#SM:**Item structure. Facet-organized, not axis-level.**
 33#XN:- Two axes per test.
 34#KJ:- Two theory-grounded facets per axis (sub-dimensions drawn from the parent construct).
 35#JK:- Eight items per facet, 16 per axis, 32 per test. This matches the NEO-PI-R standard of 8 items per facet, the structure of validated instruments.
 36#NT:- Facets are named and reported, not collapsed silently. This is the core move that separates this framework from a shallow quiz.
 37#RB:
 38#YK:**Scoring. Hierarchical, not flat.**
 39#ZH:- Facet score = mean of its 8 items, scaled 0 to 100.
 40#JH:- Axis score = mean of its 2 facet scores, scaled 0 to 100.
 41#SQ:- Prototypicality = distance from center / 70.7.
 42#BV:- Position angle = atan2, for gradation and secondary leaning.
 43#KN:- Theory-weighted (facets chosen for construct centrality), not empirically weighted (that needs pilot data we do not have).
 44#PB:
 45#PS:**Result structure.**
 46#KK:- Four quadrant types with gradation (early, mid, late) and a near-center boundary result.
 47#JH:- Each result reports the quadrant type plus the facet signature (which facets drove the axis scores). A high-Extraversion-style result can say "driven by social approach, not agency," not just "high."
 48#BT:- 14-section deep profiles, one per quadrant type, modulated by facet signature, gradation, and leaning.
 49#BY:- AI narrative layer with a deterministic 16-result fallback (4 quadrants times 4 gradation states).
 50#ZP:- Hybrid dimensional and prototypical reporting (Kerber et al. 2021), avoiding MBTI's midpoint cliff (McCrae and Costa 1989).
 51#PZ:
 52#TV:**Bias and quality handling.**
 53#WT:- Pole direction randomized per item at render time counters position bias. The bipolar two-anchor format (choosing between two statements rather than agreeing or disagreeing with one) counters acquiescence bias, the function reverse-keying serves in a unipolar format. These are two distinct mechanisms for two distinct biases.
 54#QT:- Extreme response style flag: if a respondent uses the endpoints on a disproportionate share of items, surface a soft note in the result.
 55#JT:- Internal consistency proxy: per-respondent facet spread reported as a confidence signal.
 56#XN:
 57#JP:**Item count rationale.** 32 items per test (8 per facet) matches the NEO-PI-R facet standard and sits in the validated-instrument norm. Reliability rises with item count per Spearman-Brown: at 8 per facet the expected Cronbach's alpha is .85 to .92 (strong), versus .60 to .70 at 4 per facet (marginal). At roughly 8 to 10 minutes per test this stays within personality-test norms (16Personalities holds users through 60 items; tests in this suite are taken independently). The four-test suite is 128 items total, but each test is a separate sitting.
 58#KR:
 59#PQ:**Cross-test synthesis. Structural, not just narrative.**
 60#QN:- The four tests produce 8 axis scores and 16 facet scores.
 61#ZX:- The final Solstice Identity is a computed 8-dimensional profile (radar visualization), enriched by the AI layer but not constituted by it.
 62#YR:- The synthesis is honest about overlap: where axes correlate across tests (noted in section 7), the synthesis surfaces the correlation rather than pretending independence.
 63#JN:
 64#YT:**Why the same methodology across all four.** Coherence, shared componentry, equal depth, no test accidentally weaker than another.
 65#PZ:
 66#PJ:**Theory is different per test.** Necessary, not optional.
 67#QN:- Affect is measured with affect models, not cognition models.
 68#VP:- Cognition is measured with cognitive-style models, not identity models.
 69#BS:- Identity is measured with self-concept models, not time models.
 70#MT:- Time is measured with temporal-orientation models.
 71#PR:
 72#QZ:Each test draws its two axes and four facets from the validated instruments of its own domain. The methodology transfers. The construct does not.
 73#HV:
 74#WJ:### 2.1 Honest ceiling: what is achievable without pilot data, and what is not
 75#SZ:
 76#YQ:This framework is facet-organized, theory-weighted, and structurally synthesized. That matches the structural sophistication of validated instruments like NEO-PI-R. It is the genuine ceiling for a theory-informed framework built without respondents.
 77#VB:
 78#RX:Four things stay out of reach because they require pilot data, and unlimited calendar time does not generate data:
 79#QV:- Empirical item weighting (factor loadings). We use theory-weighted facets instead.
 80#QX:- Data-driven typing (latent profile analysis). We use designed quadrants instead.
 81#WR:- Population norms (a reference distribution). Scores are unanchored; we say so.
 82#RJ:- Adaptive testing (IRT-based item selection). We use a fixed form.
 83#YX:
 84#JB:A lightly validated instrument is worse than an honestly unvalidated one, because it implies false authority. This framework claims theoretical grounding and structural honesty, not clinical or psychometric validity. That line is stated in every test doc.
 85#SR:
 86#TT:---
 87#XB:
 88#NY:## 3. Geometry note: circumplex versus plane
 89#WY:
 90#TS:Only Test 1 is a true circumplex. Affect really is circular (Russell 1980). Tests 2, 3, and 4 are two orthogonal axes forming a plane.
 91#RT:
 92#MS:The scoring math is identical either way: facet means rolled up to axis means, distance from center, angle, quadrant. The difference is only the visualization. Test 1 uses a wheel with facets as inner rings. Tests 2 to 4 use a 2x2 plane or radar with facets as sub-axes. The structure follows the construct. We do not force a circle where the construct is linear.
 93#BX:
 94#QT:Facet sub-scores appear in every result, regardless of geometry. They are what let a profile distinguish "high on this axis because of this facet, not that one."
 95#MS:
 96#WV:---
 97#ZT:
 98#YX:## 4. Per-test specifications
 99#BK:
100#QW:Each axis has 2 theory-grounded facets (8 items each). Facets named below; full definitions live in each test's doc.
101#ZS:
102#MR:| # | Theme | Name | Domain | Axis 1 (facets) | Axis 2 (facets) | Results |
103#MW:|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
104#SQ:| 1 | Solstice | SCA | Affect | Solar Height: baseline arousal, stimulation appetite | Tidal Direction: social approach, agency | Summer, Autumn, Winter, Spring |
105#QB:| 2 | Turing | MMA | Cognition | Processing Mode: deliberation preference, override tendency | Encoding Structure: entry point, working scale | Algorithm, Cipher, Gestalt, Architecture |
106#TP:| 3 | Pride | SSA | Identity | Identity Plurality: self-concept integration, contextual variation | Identity Expression: visibility preference, disclosure selectivity | Beacon, Ember, Prism, Aurora |
107#TP:| 4 | Passage of Time | TOA | Time | Temporal Orientation: past valence, future salience | Temporal Mode: scheduling preference, flow tolerance | Archivist, Navigator, Storyteller, Pioneer |
108#YQ:
109#WH:Status. Tests 1 and 2 are expanded to 32 items with the facet structure below (v0.9). Tests 3 and 4 are designed at 32 items from the start.
110#WY:
111#PK:Facet note. Test 1 Axis B facets are "social approach" (DeYoung Enthusiasm aspect) and "agency" (DeYoung Assertiveness aspect). Together they mirror the validated two-aspect structure of Big Five Extraversion. B2 was renamed twice during design ("expressive disclosure" in v0.8 overlapped Test 3; "experiential approach" in v0.9 mixed three constructs); "agency" is the correctly grounded current name.
112#QJ:
113#PP:
114#XK:---
115#PV:
116#YV:## 5. Test 3 proposal: Spectrum of Self Assessment (SSA)
117#BQ:
118#VB:**Domain.** Identity and self-expression. The personality side of Pride, not sexual orientation or gender as variables.
119#YR:
120#QX:**Why Pride fits.** Pride celebrates the plurality and authenticity of identity. A spectrum is structurally correct: people vary on how their self is organized and how it is shown, and every position is valid. The test measures those variations as personality, themed through Pride's celebration of difference.
121#QY:
122#KT:**Axis 1, Identity Plurality.** Singular and integrated versus plural and multi-faceted.
123#HW:- Construct basis: the construct anchor will be selected and verified when Test 3 is built, following the evidence standard applied to Tests 1 and 2.
124#HV:- Singular pole: one coherent core self across contexts.
125#JX:- Plural pole: many facets, different selves in different rooms, all real.
126#HT:- Neither pole is superior. Plural is reframed as complexity and range, never fragmentation.
127#XB:
128#XP:**Axis 2, Identity Expression.** Reserved and private versus expressive and visible.
129#JJ:- Construct basis: self-monitoring (Snyder 1974). Authentic living and self-disclosure (Wood et al. 2008 Authenticity Scale).
130#XR:- Reserved pole: identity held close, shown selectively or privately.
131#RM:- Expressive pole: identity made visible, disclosed, worn openly.
132#QN:- Neither pole is superior. Reserved is reframed as discernment and protection, never hiding or shame.
133#BM:
134#QP:**Four results (draft, light/spectrum imagery).**
135#XB:- Singular + Expressive: **The Beacon.** One clear identity, brightly shown.
136#MV:- Singular + Reserved: **The Ember.** One strong core, glowing within.
137#PK:- Plural + Expressive: **The Prism.** Many facets, all in the light.
138#BV:- Plural + Reserved: **The Aurora.** Many facets, shifting, partially seen.
139#QR:
140#XJ:**Open decision.** Identity Plurality × Identity Expression, or an alternative (Marcia 1966 identity statuses, or the interpersonal circumplex of agency and communion). See §8.
141#WX:
142#NQ:---
143#RS:
144#NK:## 6. Test 4 proposal: Temporal Orientation Assessment (TOA)
145#VM:
146#PZ:**Domain.** How a person relates to time. The personality side of the passage of time.
147#PT:
148#BS:**Why passage of time fits.** Time perspective is a recognized, heavily validated personality domain. The passage-of-time theme maps onto it directly. People genuinely differ on where their attention and value sits across time horizons, and how they structure time itself.
149#TJ:
150#MZ:**Axis 1, Temporal Orientation.** Past-anchored versus future-oriented.
151#MW:- Construct basis: Zimbardo and Boyd Time Perspective Inventory, ZTPI (1999). The ZTPI has five factors (Past-Positive, Past-Negative, Present-Hedonistic, Present-Fatalistic, Future), confirmed across 24 countries (Sircova et al. 2014). We use a Past composite (Past-Positive and Past-Negative averaged) as the past pole and the Future factor as the future pole. The compositing is a design choice — Sailer et al. (2014) treat the two past dimensions separately and find they contribute differently to well-being. The honesty note below addresses the information loss.
152#VK:- Past pole: value and attention on roots, memory, tradition, what has been.
153#NJ:- Future pole: value and attention on goals, possibility, what will be.
154#QH:- Honesty note 1: this axis is a composite. Past-Positive and Past-Negative are near-orthogonal in ZTPI, not opposites. Merging them is a simplification used in peer-reviewed research, but it loses texture. That texture is recovered as facet sub-scores within each result (Past-Positive vs Past-Negative, Present-Hedonistic vs Present-Fatalistic).
155#TZ:- Honesty note 2: present-oriented people land mid-axis. They are not misclassified as weakly-past-or-future. They surface via the boundary result, framed affirmatively as living in the now.
156#SH:- Alternative considered and rejected: Consideration of Future Consequences (CFC). CFC has a validated two-factor structure which would give a cleaner single axis without compositing. Rejected because CFC is decision-theoretic (how far ahead you weigh consequences) rather than humanistic, which would break tonal parity with Tests 1 to 3 and reduce the poetic passage-of-time theme to a decision-horizon instrument.
157#HJ:
158#JB:**Axis 2, Temporal Mode.** Monochronic versus polychronic.
159#SR:- Construct basis: Hall (1959) monochronic and polychronic time. Schell and Conte (2008) polychronicity validation.
160#RT:- Monochronic pole: clock-time, one thing at a time, scheduled, linear.
161#RJ:- Polychronic pole: event-time, multiple flows at once, fluid, contextual.
162#JK:- Neither pole is superior.
163#MT:- Confound honesty: monochronicity correlates with future orientation (both involve planning and scheduling). This is the same kind of cross-axis correlation as Extraversion in Tests 1/3 and Conscientiousness in Tests 2/4. The two axes are not perfectly orthogonal. Stated plainly in the test doc.
164#SK:
165#BK:**Why two axes, not ZTPI's five.** The ZTPI's full five-factor structure is richer, but breaks the suite template for one test, and five result types thins every profile and pushes past the 3-to-5 shareable-types sweet spot. Two axes keep suite coherence and synthesis evenness. The lost Present and Past-Positive/Negative variance is recovered as facet sub-scores, not lost.
166#QB:
167#RT:**Four results (draft, journey and time imagery).**
168#NV:- Past + Monochronic: **The Archivist.** Preserves, orders, keeps.
169#QX:- Future + Monochronic: **The Navigator.** Charts one course forward.
170#PY:- Past + Polychronic: **The Storyteller.** Weaves past into living present.
171#YJ:- Future + Polychronic: **The Pioneer.** Moves into the new on many threads.
172#VK:
173#JM:**Open decision.** Passage of time (recommended) versus historical-era resonance from the original GDD. The passage-of-time research above confirms the theme maps cleanly onto validated time-perspective constructs. Historical-era would overlap messily with identity and time.
174#RT:
175#MM:---
176#QN:
177#WB:## 7. Cross-suite overlap honesty
178#VY:
179#NV:Big Five is the backbone nearly everything in personality correlates with. Each test will state its own overlap. Audited loadings across the suite:
180#QS:
181#TQ:- Test 1 (SCA). Loads on Extraversion (energy) and Neuroticism (arousal).
182#TS:- Test 2 (MMA). Loads on Conscientiousness (deliberate pole) and Openness.
183#RT:- Test 3 (SSA, proposed). Loads on Openness (plurality) and Extraversion (expression). Some Extraversion overlap with Test 1, mitigated by framing Axis 2 as identity disclosure specifically, not social energy.
184#NY:- Test 4 (TOA, proposed). Loads on Conscientiousness (future) and Openness (polychronic). Some Conscientiousness overlap with Test 2, mitigated by framing as temporal structure, not general diligence.
185#HM:
186#SQ:Conceptually the four domains are distinct. At the trait level some correlation is unavoidable, because personality is not orthogonal. The contribution of each test is the facet combination and the framing, not novel dimensions. This will be stated plainly in every test doc.
187#YV:
188#MR:---
189#RS:
190#QX:## 8. Status
191#BH:
192#ZQ:Suite-level decisions locked:
193#BM:- Suite template: Option A. Tests 2 to 4 reuse Test 1's methodology (validated axes, two facets per axis, continuous scoring, four quadrant types with gradation, 14-section profiles, AI narrative, deterministic fallback, eight items per facet, seven-point bipolar Likert) with their own axes, themes, and result names. Locked v0.4.
194#JR:- Response format: Seven-point bipolar Likert. Locked across the suite.
195#QP:- Item count: 32 per test, 8 per facet. Locked across the suite.
196#PQ:- Facet structure: Two facets per axis. Locked across the suite.
197#VV:- Cross-test synthesis: Structural 8-dimensional profile with facet sub-scores. Locked.
198#JR:
199#KX:Test 3 and 4 proposals remain at draft stage (axes, facet names, result types are proposals, not locked). The 8 retained construct-anchor citations below have been reviewed for construct relevance. Full-text verification and item-level grounding will complete when each test is built.
200#MV:
201#WM:---
202#JM:
203#NJ:## 9. The synthesis
204#PX:
205#BN:With four non-overlapping domains, the final Solstice Soul synthesis combines four genuinely additive signals: how you burn (affect), how you compute (cognition), how you show (identity), and how you flow (time). This is the payoff of the domain partition. A redundant suite would re-measure the same trait four times. This suite measures four different things, so the whole is more than any part.
206#XQ:
207#BP:---
208#NZ:
209#XS:## 10. References (used only)
210#ZX:
211#XN:Test 1 and Test 2 references are documented in their own docs. This framework doc cites only the construct anchors for Tests 3 and 4.
212#SR:
213#TM:- **Russell (1980), circumplex model of affect.** *Use:* justification that Test 1 is a genuine circumplex and Tests 2 to 4 are planes (§3).
214#JH:- **Kerber, Roth and Herzberg (2021), personality types revisited.** *Use:* the hybrid dimensional and prototypical pattern shared across the suite (§2).
215#YZ:- **McCrae and Costa (1989), reinterpreting the MBTI.** *Use:* the midpoint-cliff flaw the suite avoids (§2).
216#KS:- **Snyder (1974), self-monitoring.** *Use:* anchor for Test 3 Axis 2, identity expression (§5).
217#KS:- **Wood et al. (2008), Authenticity Scale.** *Use:* corroboration for Test 3 Axis 2, authentic self-disclosure (§5).
218#XY:- **Zimbardo and Boyd (1999), Time Perspective Inventory (ZTPI).** *Use:* anchor for Test 4 Axis 1, temporal orientation. The 5-factor structure (Past-Positive, Past-Negative, Present-Hedonistic, Present-Fatalistic, Future).
219#HX:- **Sircova et al. (2014), A Global Look at Time.** *Use:* cross-cultural validation of ZTPI's 5-factor structure across 24 countries, n=12,200. Confirms the construct is robust, and confirms Past-Positive and Past-Negative are near-orthogonal (drives the honesty note about compositing).
220#YX:- **Sailer et al. (2014), time perspective and well-being.** *Use:* general ZTPI/well-being relationship. Note: this paper does not use a Past composite — it treats Past-Positive and Past-Negative as separate dimensions and finds they contribute differently to well-being. The compositing is our design choice, not a claim Sailer makes.
221#XX:- **Hall (1959), monochronic and polychronic time. Schell and Conte (2008), polychronicity and goal orientation.** *Use:* anchor for Test 4 Axis 2, temporal mode. Schell and Conte validate mono/poly as a stable individual-difference dimension. Hall is the historical origin of the construct.
222#RH:- **Marcia (1966), identity statuses.** *Use:* the strongest alternative for Test 3, named so the decision is informed (§8).
223#TK:- **Wiggins (1979), interpersonal circumplex (agency and communion).** *Use:* the most validated 2x2 alternative for Test 3, named so the decision is informed (§8).

1#TS:# Changelog
  2#KM:
  3#RN:Format: one entry per revision. Each states what changed and why. Newest first.
  4#RW:
  5#WP:## v0.17 (2026-06-18): Test 1 structural audit + 00 citation cleanup
  6#SY:
  7#XR:Why: a fresh critical audit of the complete Test 1 stack (research paper, design doc, result profiles) against the current evidence standard found five issues requiring fixes. The 00 framework doc's Test 3/4 proposal citations were also audited against the full-text paper batch and culled for relevance.
  8#XW:
  9#WN:### Test 1 changes (01, 01b, SCA-research-paper)
 10#SK:
 11#YJ:**Math error fixed.** The research paper described the prototypicality threshold (0.28) as "within about 20 points of the center on both axes." The correct figure is about 14 points for equal-offset (0.28 × 70.71 ≈ 19.8 distance; √(2d²) = 19.8 → d = 14.0). Fixed to "within about 14 points of the center on both axes (or within about 20 points on one axis while the other sits near center)."
 12#TX:
 13#QM:**A1/A2 compositing honesty note added.** Unlike Axis B, where both facets sit within DeYoung's validated two-aspect Extraversion domain, Axis A composites energetic arousal (Schimmack & Reisenzein 2002) and sensation seeking (Zuckerman 2007) — two constructs from different research traditions, never jointly validated as a single higher-order activation factor. The compositing is now stated as a design choice with facet-level reporting recovering lost texture. Same pattern as the Past-composite honesty note in 00's Test 4 proposal. Added to both 01 §8 and the research paper's facet section.
 14#BY:
 15#HS:**Intra-axis orthogonality honesty note added.** Both axes load on Big Five Extraversion — Solar Height through energy/enthusiasm facets, Tidal Direction through sociability. The quadrant boundaries are approximate, not strictly orthogonal. The hybrid dimensional/prototypical reporting pattern (types are labels on continuous scores, not discrete clusters) accommodates this. Added to research paper scoring section.
 16#VP:
 17#WX:**Three item replacements for construct clarity.**
 18#KS:
 19#RK:- A1.5: "Left with nothing to do, you feel charged / settled" → "Moving from stillness into action, you shift quickly / ease into it." The original's "idle charge" content area was a near-duplicate of A1.3's felt internal activation ("steady current running / stillness"). Replaced with transition speed — genuinely distinct from all other A1 items.
 20#YQ:
 21#KB:- A1.7: "Other people tend to read you as high-energy / low-key" → "At the end of a full day, you're still humming / winding down." The original's "external read" was a meta-perception item in a facet otherwise measuring internal felt experience, introducing a method confound. The v0.16 review kept it as a judgment call ("activation is observable so the item has validity benefit"), but for a no-data framework, unidimensionality within a facet takes priority over potential incremental criterion validity. Replaced with evening energy — still internal experience, complements A1.1's morning anchor. This overrules the v0.16 judgment call.

1#WR:# Test 1: The Solstice Cycle Assessment (SCA)
  2#KM:
  3#PT:> Status: v0.17 design document. v0.16's three judgment-call items (A1.5/A1.3 redundancy, A1.7 meta-perception confound, B2.8 competition confound) overruled for construct purity. Axis A compositing and intra-axis orthogonality honesty notes added. Threshold profile completed.
  4#WV:> Position: The solstice-themed test of the four-test Solstice Soul suite.
  5#JY:> Theme served: June Solstice (light and dark, cycles, turning points).
  6#MM:> Honesty statement: The SCA is an original, theory-informed assessment for reflection and play. Its structure is inspired by validated models of affect (Russell's circumplex) and motivation (approach and withdrawal). It is not independently validated and is not clinical. Seasonal names are an interpretive metaphor, not a claim that personality is literally seasonal. Two further honesty notes: (1) Russell's circumplex is a model of momentary affect, a state model. We use its structure to organize trait-like dispositions, a move supported by the trait-affect literature but stated here openly rather than implied. (2) The June solstice is summer in the Northern Hemisphere and winter in the Southern. The SCA uses internal, hemisphere-neutral seasons and does not assume a hemisphere.
  7#HN:
  8#ZR:---
  9#JT:
 10#XJ:## 1. The name
 11#TJ:
 12#PR:**The Solstice Cycle Assessment (SCA).** Locked v0.3.
 13#BQ:
 14#YT:"Assessment" signals a serious instrument (NEO-PI, TEMPS, BIS/BAS). "Cycle" signals the circumplex foundation and the solstice's cyclical nature. "Solstice" ties it to theme and suite.
 15#RJ:
 16#RX:The in-game UI may use the friendlier "Solstice Compass" label, but the framework name is SCA.
 17#HX:
 18#NM:---
 19#YT:
 20#ZM:## 2. Theoretical foundation (each source states its use)
 21#RJ:
 22#SV:Structure comes from validated models. Texture comes from classical and archetypal ones. The boundary is stated explicitly. That boundary is what makes the framework credible rather than pseudo-scientific.
 23#NV:
 24#MH:### 2.1 Structural sources (define what we measure)
 25#XW:
 26#XV:- **Russell (1980), Circumplex Model of Affect.** Affect is organized on a circle defined by two orthogonal axes, activation and valence. *Use:* core geometric anchor. A circle is the correct shape for anything seasonal, because seasons are cyclical.
 27#HM:- **Yik, Russell and Steiger (2011), 12-Point Affect Circumplex Scales.** Validated instrument for the circumplex. *Use:* evidence that the circular structure is measurable, not just conceptual.
 28#HX:- **Schimmack and Reisenzein (2002), energetic arousal.** Demonstrated that energetic arousal is a distinct activation type, not a mixture of valence and general activation. *Use:* grounds Axis A's high pole (brightness) in an independently validated construct. The energetic arousal concept originates with Thayer (1989), but our direct source is Schimmack and Reisenzein.
 29#ST:- **Carver and White (1994), BIS/BAS scales.** Validated motivational dimension: approach and withdrawal are orthogonal systems, not opposite poles of one. *Use:* grounds Axis B (Tidal Direction) in approach and withdrawal.
 30#ZM:
 31#KM:### 2.2 Textural sources (define how we describe)
 32#JQ:
 33#SK:- **Big Five and HEXACO.** The consensus dimensional baseline. *Use:* reality check that our axes do not reinvent variance already captured elsewhere. Stated overlap in §8.
 34#WV:
 35#ZX:### 2.3 Why four types is defensible
 36#MV:
 37#MN:- **Gerlach, Farb, Revelle and Amaral (2018, Nature Human Behaviour).** Gaussian mixture models with density-based significance testing on roughly 1.5 million people yielded four replicable types (Average, Reserved, Role-Model, Self-Centered). *Use:* empirical defense that four types can be data-supported, not arbitrary.
 38#HJ:- **Kerber, Roth and Herzberg (2021), Personality types revisited.** Argues for a hybrid prototypical and dimensional representation. *Use:* justifies our scoring pattern. Dimensional underneath, labelled type on top.
 39#MS:
 40#HQ:### 2.4 Response-format sources (decide how we ask)
 41#BH:
 42#QY:- **McCrae and Costa (1989), reinterpreting the MBTI.** MBTI's binary dichotomies show no bimodality. Dichotomizing discards about 26 to 32 percent of information and inflates reliability. *Use:* reason to reject binary A/B forced choice.
 43#MX:- **Schulte, Holling and Burkner (2020).** Pure forced-choice yields ipsative scores that cannot compare people, even with 30 traits. *Use:* reason to reject forced-choice scoring.
 44#QS:- **Sun, Schmidt and Henry (2025), "Don't Let Your Likert Scales Grow Up To Be Visual Analog Scales."** Visual analogue scales (0 to 100 sliders) do not outperform Likert and add measurement error, especially with few items. *Use:* primary reason to reject the slider format proposed in v0.1.
 45#VV:- **Chang (1994), four-point and six-point Likert scales.** *Use:* grounds the choice of seven points (at least five, with strong discrimination and low cognitive load).
 46#XQ:- **Gosling, Rentfrow and Swann (2003), TIPI.** Ultra-short scales (two items per dimension) are too thin for acceptable reliability. *Use:* sets the item-count floor.
 47#JV:- **Spearman-Brown prophecy formula.** Reliability rises monotonically with item count, with diminishing returns past 8 per facet. *Use:* grounds the 8-items-per-facet standard, where expected Cronbach's alpha reaches the .85 to .92 strong band.
 48#BY:
 49#RY:### 2.5 Facet grounding (added v0.6)
 50#QW:
 51#WY:The facets under each axis are grounded in validated sub-constructs, not invented.
 52#NM:
 53#KH:**Axis A facets.**
 54#NW:- **A1 Baseline Arousal:** Schimmack and Reisenzein (2002), energetic arousal. The tonic activation set-point, felt as energy versus tiredness. Demonstrated to be a distinct activation type, not reducible to valence plus general activation. The energetic arousal construct originates with Thayer (1989), but our direct source is Schimmack and Reisenzein.
 55#YV:- **A2 Stimulation Appetite:** Zuckerman (2007), Sensation Seeking Scale. The preferred level of varied, novel, and intense stimulation. The SSS-V has been validated across hundreds of studies with replicated four-subscale structure and discriminant validity. The general construct originates in Zuckerman (1979), but our direct source is the 2007 validation review.
 56#XN:
 57#YN:**Axis B facets.**
 58#JN:- **B1 Social Approach:** DeYoung, Quilty and Peterson (2007), Big Five Aspect Scales, Enthusiasm aspect. Sociability, affiliation, positive emotion toward others.
 59#KN:- **B2 Agency:** DeYoung, Quilty and Peterson (2007), Big Five Aspect Scales, Assertiveness aspect. Proactive agency, action initiation, dominance, drive toward impact. Together B1 and B2 mirror the validated two-aspect structure of Extraversion (Enthusiasm and Assertiveness), with Carver and White (1994) BAS subtypes (Drive, Reward-Responsiveness) as corroborating split.
 60#HQ:
 61#WX:Naming note. B2 was renamed twice. v0.8 named it "expressive disclosure" (overlapped Test 3 identity expression). v0.9 named it "experiential approach" (mixed three constructs: agency, experiential engagement, novelty seeking, while citing only the first). v0.12 renamed it "agency," the narrower construct DeYoung's Assertiveness aspect actually validates. Axis B now maps exactly to DeYoung's two-aspect structure of Extraversion.
 62#RJ:
 63#YV:Honesty note. The facet split is theory-grounded, but the specific SCA facet scales are not independently validated. That line is restated in section 10.
 64#XZ:
 65#WP:Every source above is used. No unused citations are listed.
 66#JQ:
 67#TH:---
 68#RT:
 69#YQ:## 3. Why the framework fits the solstice
 70#YY:
 71#RP:The solstice is a point on the yearly cycle of light that produces the seasons. The SCA places a person on exactly such a cycle: Axis A measures activation (metaphorically, brightness), and the result is a phase on that cycle. No other jam theme has this clean a mapping to a validated structure.
 72#SV:
 73#QP:A note on the metaphor. The solstices are the cycle's extremes (most and least light), and they are where the cycle turns, the sun stands still and reverses. The equinoxes are the cycle's balance points (equal light and dark). We use this distinction in the result structure: the Axis-A extremes carry the solstice poetry; the wheel's center is the equinox position.
 74#HQ:
 75#NS:| Solstice essence | How the framework embodies it |
 76#JB:|---|---|
 77#NZ:| A point on a cycle | Result is a phase on a wheel, not a flat category |
 78#SX:| Light and dark (as metaphor) | Axis A is bright versus dim, the evocative label for high versus low affective activation |
 79#KY:| The turning point, where the cycle reverses | This lives at the Axis-A extremes (Summer and Winter), which carry the solstice poetry |
 80#XX:| Longest and shortest day | Summer (Bright) and Winter (Dim) are the high and low poles of the self's cycle |
 81#ZT:| Balance and transition | The near-center result is the equinox position, a threshold between seasons, not the solstice |
 82#YR:
 83#NK:Honesty note on Spring and Autumn. They are the transitional seasons, and we place them by current activation state, not trajectory: Spring is low-activation (energy still gathering), Autumn is high-activation (energy still abundant). Their trajectory (rising or falling) is captured by the angle gradation, not the axis. This is a designer reading grounded in the activation construct.
 84#WR:
 85#VQ:---
 86#KR:
 87#MS:## 4. The dimensions measured
 88#VS:
 89#WN:Two orthogonal continuous axes, each 0 to 100.
 90#QT:
 91#TZ:**Dimension A, Solar Height** (affective activation, energetic intensity).
 92#YB:- Construct basis: Russell circumplex activation axis. Schimmack and Reisenzein (2002) energetic arousal. Bright and Dim are evocative labels for high and low activation, inspired by the solstice's light cycle but not literal light measurements.
 93#HY:- High pole, Bright: radiant, high-energy, intense.
 94#ZY:- Low pole, Dim: quiet, low-arousal, still, interior. Reframed as depth and calm, never depression.
 95#MS:
 96#XK:**Dimension B, Tidal Direction** (motivational orientation, energy flow).
 97#QW:- Construct basis: BAS approach versus BIS withdrawal (Carver and White 1994).
 98#ZJ:- High pole, Outward: energy moving toward the world. Opening, engaging, approach-oriented.
 99#MY:- Low pole, Inward: energy drawing toward the interior. Conserving, gathering, reflective.
100#SR:
101#RH:Each quadrant embodies a seasonal archetype. The person is always a point on the wheel, never forced into a binary.
102#PJ:
103#TH:---
104#NJ:
105#MS:## 5. The four result types
106#HT:
107#HX:| | **Outward** | **Inward** |
108#ZX:|---|---|---|
109#HJ:| **Bright** | ☀️ Summer, The Zenith | 🍂 Autumn, The Turning |
110#TP:| **Dim** | 🌱 Spring, The Greening | ❄️ Winter, The Deep |
111#YX:
112#JZ:Full 14-section profiles live in `01b-solstice-result-profiles.md`. Modeled on bigfive-test.com facet depth and mypersonality.net type profiles.
113#PP:
114#YX:One-line essences:
115#HS:- ☀️ **Summer, The Zenith** (Bright + Outward). Abundant, radiant, generative. The high point of the cycle, peak activation.
116#BP:- 🍂 **Autumn, The Turning** (Bright + Inward). The harvest self. Luminous but consolidating. Intensity gathering for release.
117#HB:- ❄️ **Winter, The Deep** (Dim + Inward). Richest in stillness and interiority. Quiet, rooted, renewing. Reframed as depth, never deficit.
118#SN:- 🌱 **Spring, The Greening** (Dim + Outward). Tender, persistent new growth. Adaptive, hopeful, renewing. The courage of softness.
119#YR:
120#MJ:Why Autumn is Bright plus Inward: autumn is the harvest, still luminous (golden hour, peak color) but with the sap turning inward. The archetype is intensity gathering itself for release. This avoids "autumn equals sad" and keeps all four types affirming.
121#QY:
122#HW:**Result label convention (locked v0.3): season-primary, archetype as subtitle.** The results screen reads `🍂 Autumn: The Turning`. The season is the headline. It answers the question the test asks and is the shareable unit ("I got Autumn, what did you get?"). The archetype is the evocative tagline for depth and texture. This mirrors bigfive-test.com ("Agreeableness" headline plus description) and mypersonality.net ("INTJ" plus type name).
123#WY:
124#MM:---
125#YB:
126#BP:## 6. Methodology and scoring
127#XB:
128#ZP:**Step 1, collect.** 32 responses, each 1 to 7. Four facets, 8 items each: A1, A2 (Axis A), B1, B2 (Axis B).
129#HP:
130#XY:**Step 2, direction-normalize.** For each item, the raw response is mapped so a higher value always means more Bright (Axis A) or more Outward (Axis B). At render time, pole direction is randomized (which pole appears on the left versus the right), so the respondent cannot default to one side of the screen. This counters position bias.
131#WP:
132#BP:**Step 3, facet scores.**
133#JB:- A1 = mean of normalized A1 items, scaled 0 to 100. 0 is low baseline arousal, 100 is high.
134#WW:- A2 = mean of normalized A2 items, scaled 0 to 100. 0 is low stimulation appetite, 100 is high.
135#KR:- B1 = mean of normalized B1 items, scaled 0 to 100. 0 is socially withdrawn, 100 is socially approachful.
136#HV:- B2 = mean of normalized B2 items, scaled 0 to 100. 0 is receptive, 100 is agentic.
137#QS:
138#SH:**Step 4, axis scores.**
139#WP:- A (Solar Height) = mean of A1 and A2, scaled 0 to 100. 0 is Dim, 100 is Bright.
140#SV:- B (Tidal Direction) = mean of B1 and B2, scaled 0 to 100. 0 is Inward, 100 is Outward.
141#WX:
142#HV:**Step 5, locate on the wheel.** Center is (50, 50).
143#YQ:- Quadrant (your season) from the signs of A−50 and B−50.
144#PQ:  - A>50, B>50: Summer
145#QM:  - A>50, B<50: Autumn
146#TW:  - A<50, B<50: Winter
147#WW:  - A<50, B>50: Spring
148#XH:- Prototypicality r = distance from center / 70.7. Higher means more clearly that season. Lower means more between.
149#QX:- Phase angle = atan2(B−50, A−50). Maps to an exact position. Used for gradation (early, mid, late) and secondary leaning.
150#PY:
151#MV:**Step 6, classify.**
152#JT:- r ≥ 0.28: report primary season plus gradation plus leaning, plus the facet signature (which facets drove the axis scores). The extreme Axis-A results (most Bright, most Dim) additionally carry a solstice beat in the narrative, because those are the literal solstice positions on the wheel.
153#JH:- r < 0.28 (near center or near an axis): report the **Threshold** result, the equinox position. "You sit at a threshold, the equinox point, the pause between X and Y where energy and stillness, outward and inward, are in balance." Facet signature still reported. This resolves gracefully instead of forcing an arbitrary call.
154#QH:
155#KH:This is the hybrid dimensional and prototypical pattern Kerber et al. (2021) advocate, with facet-level reporting per the v0.9 suite standard. It avoids MBTI's central flaw, the false cliff at the midpoint. A person at 51 versus 49 gets a graduated reading, not a different identity.
156#TT:
157#JZ:---
158#TV:
159#WV:## 7. Question format and response scale
160#ZB:
161#VR:**Format: a scenario stem plus a seven-point bipolar Likert between two anchor statements.**
162#VQ:
163#SV:```
164#WT:"When nothing demands your attention, your mind…"
165#BS:[ Stays active • • • • • • Settles into quiet ]
166#WS:                                       tap a pip
167#XW:```
168#BT:
169#RT:Each item shows two anchor statements (the two poles of the axis) with seven discrete, clickable segments between them. The midpoint is neutral. Pole direction alternates per item to counter position bias; the bipolar two-anchor format itself counters acquiescence bias.
170#HM:
171#BK:**Why a seven-point bipolar Likert, not a percentage slider.**
172#VT:The v0.1 draft proposed a 0 to 100 slider. The literature forced a reversal.
173#TM:- Sun, Schmidt and Henry (2025): sliders do not outperform Likert and add measurement error with few items.
174#RT:
175#MR:Decisive practical point: every validated personality inventory uses Likert. NEO-PI-R, BFI-2, HEXACO-PI-R, TIPI, IPIP. None use sliders. Likert is more familiar, more mobile-friendly (discrete taps, not dragging), and more reproducible (better test-retest). The bipolar two-statement form keeps the vivid either-or feel the theme wants while behaving psychometrically like a Likert or semantic-differential item.
176#QN:
177#QR:Why seven points: Chang (1994) and the scale-points literature favor at least five. Seven gives strong discrimination with low cognitive load. A symmetric midpoint avoids forced dichotomizing, the MBTI flaw.
178#VY:
179#NP:The wheel visualization is retained as a **results reveal only** (plot the point, animate into the quadrant). Keeping it out of the input phase avoids anchoring and contaminating responses.
180#QS:
181#SJ:Explicitly avoided: binary A/B forced choice (no bimodality, discards information, inflates reliability). Pure forced-choice and ipsative scoring (Schulte et al. 2020). Zero to 100 sliders as the input mechanism.
182#NT:
183#WB:---
184#NB:
185#BZ:## 8. Number of questions
186#HN:
187#PQ:**32 items, facet-organized.** 2 axes, 2 facets per axis, 8 items per facet. Matches the NEO-PI-R facet standard.
188#XH:
189#TB:**Why 32.** Reliability rises with items-per-facet per Spearman-Brown. At 8 per facet the expected Cronbach's alpha is .85 to .92 (strong), versus .60 to .70 at 4 per facet (marginal). Roughly 8 to 10 minutes, within personality-test norms. Tests in the suite are taken independently, so per-test length is what matters per sitting.
190#JM:
191#YK:**Facet structure.**
192#KQ:- Axis A, Solar Height: A1 Baseline Arousal (tonic activation, your default energy set-point), A2 Stimulation Appetite (preferred input and activity level).
193#XN:
194#XZ:Honesty note. Unlike Axis B, whose two facets sit within a single validated domain (DeYoung's two-aspect Extraversion), Axis A composites two constructs from different research traditions — energetic arousal and sensation seeking — without a jointly validated higher-order activation factor. The compositing is a design choice. The facet signature recovers lost texture by reporting which sub-component drove the axis score.
195#KP:- Axis B, Tidal Direction: B1 Social Approach (toward or away from people, DeYoung Enthusiasm aspect), B2 Agency (proactive action and initiation versus receptive response, DeYoung Assertiveness aspect). B2 was renamed from "experiential approach" (v0.9) and from "expressive disclosure" (v0.8); both earlier names were either off-construct or overlapping with Test 3. The two facets now map exactly to DeYoung's validated two-aspect structure of Extraversion.
196#ZR:
197#MQ:**Item-writing rules applied.** Vary exactly one facet per item. True antonym poles on a single dimension. Neutral language (behavior, not virtue). No transparent giveaways. Gender-neutral and identity-agnostic. Both poles affirming. Two bias controls: pole direction randomized at render time (counters position bias), and the bipolar two-anchor format where respondents choose between two statements rather than agreeing or disagreeing with one (counters acquiescence bias, the function reverse-keying serves in a unipolar format).
198#JR:
199#WK:### Facet A1: Baseline Arousal (8 items)
200#MV:
201#BN:All items vary the tonic activation set-point. Each item targets a distinct content area (waking state, default attention, inner current, default readiness, transition speed, somatic primed-ness, evening energy, comparative frame) rather than paraphrasing one idea. No agency, social, or stimulation-volume language.
202#JM:
203#HT:| # | Scenario stem | Bright pole (high activation) | Dim pole (low activation) |
204#RB:|---|---|---|---|
205#JY:| A1.1 | When you wake, you're… | "Already at full charge." | "Still coming online, quietly." |
206#MY:| A1.2 | When nothing demands your attention, your mind… | "Stays active." | "Settles into quiet." |
207#RN:| A1.3 | Inside you, there's… | "A steady current running." | "A stillness." |
208#YX:| A1.4 | Your default state is closer to… | "Readiness." | "Rest." |
209#RS:| A1.5 | Moving from stillness into action, you… | "Shift quickly." | "Ease into it." |
210#QT:| A1.6 | Your body at rest is… | "Primed." | "Deeply still." |
211#HR:| A1.7 | At the end of a full day, you're… | "Still humming." | "Winding down." |
212#ZV:| A1.8 | Compared to most people, you run… | "Hotter." | "Cooler." |
213#ZP:
214#JP:### Facet A2: Stimulation Appetite (8 items)
215#XJ:
216#RZ:All items vary preferred stimulation level. Each item targets a distinct content area (sensory intensity, environmental density, pace, information input volume, free-time scheduling density, boredom susceptibility, variety, comparative frame). No sensory-processing-sensitivity language (no "drains me", "overwhelmed"), no energy-variability language (no "spiky", "peaks"), no agency language (no "actively doing", "getting things done").
217#BB:
218#XJ:| # | Scenario stem | Bright pole (seeks stimulation) | Dim pole (limits stimulation) |
219#WT:|---|---|---|---|
220#YP:| A2.1 | The sensory intensity you prefer is… | "Intense." | "Gentle." |
221#SK:| A2.2 | You prefer your environment… | "Busy and full." | "Sparse and open." |
222#BH:| A2.3 | The pace you prefer is… | "Fast." | "Slow." |
223#NM:| A2.4 | How much information and input you want coming at you is… | "A lot." | "A little." |
224#KM:| A2.5 | Your free time, you prefer… | "Packed with things to do." | "Open and unscheduled." |
225#VX:| A2.6 | When nothing much is happening, you feel… | "Restless. You want more." | "Content. The quiet is fine." |
226#ZV:| A2.7 | You prefer things… | "Changing and varied." | "Steady and uniform." |
227#XH:| A2.8 | Compared to most people, you run on… | "More stimulation." | "Less stimulation." |
228#PR:
229#RQ:### Facet B1: Social Approach (8 items)
230#QP:

1#WY:# The Solstice Cycle Assessment
  2#KM:
  3#QB:## A personality framework built on how you burn, how you move, and where you land on the cycle of light
  4#RW:
  5#HH:---
  6#SY:
  7#JB:The summer solstice is the longest day of the year. The sun climbs to its highest point, pauses at the apex, and reverses direction. The winter solstice is the opposite , the longest night, the deepest dark, the turning point back toward light. These are not just astronomical events. They are metaphors for how people are.
  8#XW:
  9#KV:Some people live at their summer solstice , bright, outward, abundant, running at full charge. Others live at their winter solstice , deep, quiet, interior, their richest life unfolding in stillness. Most people fall somewhere between these poles, and somewhere between inward and outward, on a cycle that turns through four recognizable seasons of the self.
 10#SK:
 11#MP:The Solstice Cycle Assessment maps you onto that cycle. It measures two things: how bright your characteristic energy burns, and which direction it tends to flow. From those two coordinates, it places you in one of four seasons. Every position is valid. There is no bad season. The test is built on a specific body of research , on how people experience activation, on how motivation works in the brain, on why personality instruments that force you into boxes lose real information. This article explains what the test measures, why it was designed the way it was, what each result means, and what the research actually says about each piece of the framework.
 12#TX:
 13#SV:---
 14#BY:
 15#RW:## What the test measures
 16#VP:
 17#WJ:Two dimensions. Each scored from 0 to 100. Neither is better than the other. Together they place you somewhere on a wheel.
 18#KS:
 19#VT:**Solar Height** is your characteristic energy level , how bright you burn at baseline. This is not your mood at this moment. It is your dispositional activation: when nothing is demanding anything of you, are you humming or settled? Do you wake at full charge, or do you come online slowly? The concept comes from the most validated model of how people experience affect , Russell's (1980) circumplex, a two-dimensional circle on which all affective states can be located. One of its two axes is arousal, the dimension from sleepiness to high activation. Russell demonstrated this structure using four independent scaling methods in the same paper , circular ordering, multidimensional scaling, unidimensional scaling on pleasure and arousal dimensions, and analysis of 343 people's self-reports , and all four methods converged. The arousal axis is not a metaphor. It is a measurable, replicable dimension of human experience.
 20#YQ:
 21#MR:The SCA labels the high end *Bright* and the low end *Dim*, but these are evocative names for high and low activation. Bright is energized, alert, internally active. Dim is calm, quiet, still. Dim is not depression. It is depth and restoration. The test measures whether you tend toward one or the other, and to what degree.
 22#ZP:
 23#YX:**Tidal Direction** is where your energy tends to flow , outward toward the world and other people, or inward toward your interior and your own reflection. This axis comes from Carver and White's (1994) work on the brain's motivational systems. They developed a self-report instrument measuring two systems that Gray (1981) had identified: the Behavioral Activation System, which responds to reward and drives approach behavior, and the Behavioral Inhibition System, which responds to punishment and drives withdrawal and vigilance. The critical finding for the SCA is that these two systems are independent , Carver and White state explicitly that they are "presumed to be orthogonal" (p. 320), and their data, from four studies including actual laboratory experiments where people anticipated real reward or punishment, confirmed that people can be high in both, low in both, or any combination. Approach and withdrawal are not opposite ends of one dimension. They are two separate dimensions, and a person's characteristic balance between them is what the SCA measures on a single continuous scale.
 24#KW:
 25#TN:The SCA labels the high end *Outward* , energy flowing toward engagement, action, and social connection. The low end is *Inward* , energy flowing toward reflection, interiority, and conservation. Neither is better.
 26#HK:
 27#NP:Because Russell's circumplex and Carver and White's motivational systems are independently validated structures, combining them into a two-axis framework is not arbitrary. The SCA uses one axis from the affect literature and one from the motivational literature, places them orthogonally, and maps a person's position on the resulting plane. The four quadrants of that plane are the four seasons. The wheel is the natural geometry of the circumplex. The seasons are the interpretive layer.
 28#HQ:
 29#MW:---
 30#ZM:
 31#VT:## The four seasons
 32#JQ:
 33#YT:Each season is a specific combination of an energy level and a direction. Each comes with a full profile describing what that combination tends to look like in real life. The profiles are archetypes , patterns that emerge from the axis geometry, not empirical clusters discovered by fitting a model to data. But the literature independently supports that a small number of personality types in the 3 to 5 range is replicable across large datasets. Gerlach, Farb, Revelle, and Amaral (2018) found four types across 1.5 million respondents using a density-based significance method that filters out spurious cluster solutions. Kerber, Roth, and Herzberg (2021) reviewed 19 prior studies and ran three different clustering algorithms on a dataset of 22,820 people, finding five robust types. The SCA's four types are theory-derived, not data-clustered, but the empirical literature independently confirms that four sits in the viable range. The test reports continuous scores *and* a type label , the type is the interpretation, not the measurement.
 34#WV:
 35#PH:### ☀️ Summer , The Zenith
 36#MV:
 37#PB:Bright and Outward. High energy turned fully toward the world.
 38#BN:
 39#BM:**The archetype.** Summer is the peak of the cycle. These are people whose energy burns high and flows outward. When they enter a room, the temperature tends to rise , not through force, but through sheer generative presence. Things bloom around them because they bring light and momentum. They are most themselves in motion: making, connecting, starting, giving.
 40#ZK:
 41#SJ:The gift is abundance. The shadow is the same: a sun that never sets burns out. Summer people tend to equate stillness with failure or low mood, and they may underestimate how much restoration they actually need. They recover energy through engagement rather than withdrawal, which works until it doesn't.
 42#XN:
 43#SN:**Motivations.** To express fully , to bring what is inside into the world without dampening it. To generate and start things. To live in the center of life rather than at its edges. To feel and be felt, vividly.
 44#PB:
 45#XY:**How they behave.** High, visible energy. They are often the one initiating conversations, plans, and activities. They think out loud and decide in motion. They expand social situations , more people, more activity, more yes. Their mood is readable, and it tends to influence the room. They recover energy through engagement.
 46#TJ:
 47#SV:**Strengths.** Magnetism and warmth. People feel lit up around them. Generative drive , they start and ship. Courage of expression and low fear of visibility. An ability to make others feel included and energized. Resilience through action , they move through difficulty by doing.
 48#BY:
 49#RX:**Blind spots.** Equating stillness with failure or low mood. Overcommitting , saying yes past their real capacity. Underestimating quieter people's depth, and their own need for it. Believing that intensity equals commitment or love. Burning out and reading the exhaustion as a personal failure rather than a signal to rest.
 50#QW:
 51#XW:**Growth.** Build deliberate recovery into the rhythm. Practice the power of one well-chosen no. Learn that withdrawal is a skill, not a deficit. Let others hold the spotlight , practice being warmed rather than always warming.
 52#NM:
 53#TM:**Relationships.** Summer people bring warmth, generosity, and momentum to their relationships. They may overwhelm more inward partners and misread slowness as disinterest. They need people who can meet their energy and remind them to rest. The growth edge is learning to love that can hold their quiet, not just their shine.
 54#YJ:
 55#XB:**Work.** They thrive in dynamic, visible, generative roles , launches, starts, rallying teams, pitching, leading from the front. Risk: starting more than they finish, and mistaking busyness for output. Ideal environments offer high autonomy and energy, with recovery explicitly built in.
 56#XN:
 57#XY:**Decision-making.** Fast, intuitive, often in dialogue with others. They decide by doing , action clarifies. Risk: deciding from peak emotion. Major calls benefit from a 24-hour pause. Strength: they do not get stuck in analysis.
 58#KR:
 59#RZ:**Under stress.** The signature is acceleration , more activity, more volume, more taking-on. They may radiate stress outward, affecting those near them. Recovery requires what is hardest for them: stopping, dimming, going inward. Watch for irritability and depletion disguised as "just busy."
 60#HQ:
 61#MH:**Communication.** Direct, expressive, warm, often high-volume. They inspire and mobilize well. Growth: make space for silence. Not every silence needs filling. Listen for the people who speak after they stop.
 62#RJ:
 63#HB:**The complementary season.** Winter. Summer's wholeness lives in the part of the cycle they tend to skip , Winter's stillness, depth, and restoration. The sun that rests returns brighter. The deepest growth is permission to dim without fear.
 64#XZ:
 65#RB:---
 66#JQ:
 67#BP:### 🍂 Autumn , The Turning
 68#RT:
 69#TS:Bright and Inward. High energy that has turned inward , intensity gathering itself for release.
 70#YY:
 71#QY:**The archetype.** Autumn is the harvest self. These people carry real intensity, but it moves inward. They are the golden hour: warm and lit, yet drawing the sap down toward the root. They do not lack energy. They are directing it , gathering what matters, distilling it, deciding what to keep and what to let fall.
 72#SV:
 73#PB:Where Summer burns outward, Autumn consolidates. They feel deeply and have learned to hold it, refine it, and release what no longer serves. The gift is intensity with judgment. The shadow is that withdrawal can masquerade as wisdom , sometimes it is avoidance. They may be misread as distant when they are in fact carrying a great deal.
 74#HQ:
 75#MK:Why is Autumn placed at Bright rather than Dim? Astronomically, autumn is decreasing light, and one could argue it belongs at the low-activation end. But energetically, autumn is still abundant , the harvest is full, the colors are at peak intensity, the warmth has not yet left. The SCA places seasons by their current energy state, not their trajectory. Autumn's trajectory , the turning toward winter , is captured by the angle gradation, not the axis. This is a design choice grounded in the activation construct.
 76#JW:
 77#XB:**Motivations.** To distill meaning from experience , to keep only what is true. To honor the full cycle, including release. To hold intensity without being run by it. To integrate, not just accumulate.
 78#PX:
 79#MP:**How they behave.** Warm but selective , they go deep with a few. They process before they share; their output is considered. They let go of roles, identities, and relationships more readily than most. They are comfortable with endings and transitions. Their intensity is real, but private , others may underestimate it.
 80#KB:
 81#WR:**Strengths.** Discernment , they know what to keep and what to release. Depth without coldness, warmth without diffusion. Comfort with change, loss, and transition. Mature self-awareness , they have integrated a lot. The ability to hold paradox: bright and inward at once.
 82#YR:
 83#SX:**Blind spots.** Withdrawal can masquerade as wisdom. Releasing too much , cutting things prematurely. Being misread as fine or distant when carrying a lot. Nostalgia tipping into stuckness. Withholding warmth as self-protection.
 84#WR:
 85#QK:**Growth.** Distinguish discernment from avoidance , "am I letting go, or am I leaving?" Share the harvest , what has been gathered is meant to feed others. Let people in on the intensity rather than refining it alone. Resist the romance of melancholy.
 86#KR:
 87#VZ:**Relationships.** They offer rare depth, loyalty, and the courage to face hard truths together. Partners may feel held but also kept at a refined distance. They thrive with people who can meet their interiority without flinching. Growth: let yourself be known, not just understood.
 88#VS:
 89#KH:**Work.** Excellent at synthesis, editing, strategy, and finishing. They shine in roles requiring judgment and integration. Risk: over-refining , shipping late because it is "not ready." Ideal environments offer autonomous depth-work with meaningful collaboration.
 90#QT:
 91#XZ:**Decision-making.** Deliberate, values-driven, comfortable with trade-offs. They decide well when they trust their discernment. Risk: analysis loops , deciding by elimination rather than commitment. Strength: they rarely make reckless calls.
 92#JZ:
 93#JT:**Under stress.** The signature is pulling inward and refining harder , overthinking, withdrawal. They may become quietly heavy. Recovery requires movement, release, and trusted conversation , getting it out. Watch for isolation disguised as "processing."
 94#MS:
 95#HS:**Communication.** Precise, considered, sometimes sparing. They say less and mean more. Growth: do not make people guess , share the warmth being refined. Their words land. Use that power generously.
 96#ZT:
 97#ZB:**The complementary season.** Spring. Autumn's wholeness lives in re-engagement , Spring's tender, outward, hopeful new growth. Having learned to let go, the next mastery is beginning again, and trusting it.
 98#BP:
 99#SJ:---
100#SR:
101#VJ:### ❄️ Winter , The Deep
102#PJ:
103#BQ:Dim and Inward. Richest in stillness and interiority. Power that is quiet, rooted, and renewing.
104#NJ:
105#BH:**The archetype.** Winter is the longest night. These people find their richest territory in interior life , depth, clarity, and restoration emerge in stillness, not because they lack energy but because their energy is concentrated rather than dispersed. They are the part of the cycle where the seed does its essential work in the dark.
106#HT:
107#NX:Winter is reframed, always, as depth and renewal. Never deficit. Winter's power is quiet and rooted: they see clearly because they are not dazzled by surface light. They endure because they have learned to rest. The world tends to undervalue stillness. Winter's gift is proving how generative it actually is.
108#YQ:
109#KZ:**Motivations.** To understand deeply , truth over performance. To protect and tend what is essential. To restore, root, and renew. To be real, not reactive.
110#WY:
111#SX:**How they behave.** Low, steady output , long horizon. They observe more than they emit and remember what others miss. They are comfortable alone and recharge in solitude and slowness. Their commitments are few but deep, and loyal once given. Their presence is calming and clarifying for others.
112#QJ:
113#KZ:**Strengths.** Depth of insight and clear seeing. Steadiness, endurance, patience. Independence and self-sufficiency. A calming, grounding presence. The ability to renew themselves through difficulty.
114#BJ:
115#QX:**Blind spots.** Staying in the cold too long , withdrawal tipping into isolation. Under-asserting , their depth goes unseen and unmet. Mistaking slowness for incapability, theirs or others'. Holding too tightly to the interior and not emerging. Reading high-energy people as superficial.
116#BK:
117#HQ:**Growth.** Practice emergent action before feeling "ready." Let yourself be seen and supported , receiving is a skill. Share your insights , the world needs what you see. Distinguish rest from hiding.
118#RM:
119#KN:**Relationships.** Winter people offer rare loyalty, depth, and steadiness. They need people who respect their slowness and solitude. Risk: partners feel shut out , the interior must be translated. Growth: initiate connection, not just respond to it.
120#XM:
121#RY:**Work.** Excellent at deep, focused, long-horizon work. They shine in analysis, research, craft, and anything requiring sustained attention. Risk: invisibility , their best work may go uncredited. Ideal environments offer protected focus time, low meetings, and a culture that honors depth.
122#JQ:
123#HM:**Decision-making.** Slow, thorough, high-quality. They decide once and well, with low regret. Risk: over-deliberation , missing time-sensitive windows. Strength: their calls tend to hold up over time.
124#KZ:
125#KT:**Under stress.** The signature is withdrawing further, going quieter, carrying it alone. They may seem fine while struggling. Recovery requires gentle re-engagement and trusted warmth , not forced socializing. Watch for the long night becoming permanent. Set a thaw date.
126#WV:
127#PP:**Communication.** Considered, economical, often written better than spoken. When they speak, it matters. Growth: do not wait until it is perfect. Say the half-formed thing. Their listening is a gift , name it for others.
128#YX:
129#YB:**The complementary season.** Summer. Winter's wholeness lives in emergence , Summer's full, outward, radiant expression. The seed's whole purpose is the bloom. The deepest growth is daring to take up space.

133#NW:### 🌱 Spring , The Greening
134#QZ:
135#XP:Dim and Outward. Tender, persistent new growth moving outward into the world. Adaptive, hopeful, renewing.
136#NQ:
137#BZ:**The archetype.** Spring moves outward but softly , not with Summer's blaze, but with the green persistence of the first shoot through cold ground. Their energy is modest in wattage but extraordinary in resilience. They adapt, renew, and begin again. They are proof that tender things are strong.
138#KK:
139#NB:Spring is the courage of softness. These people engage the world without needing to dominate it. They are the friend who resurfaces after every winter, the one who tries again. The gift is renewal , for themselves and everyone they touch.
140#XS:
141#HX:Like Autumn, Spring's placement follows the energy-state logic: spring's activation is still low , the shoots are tender, the warmth not yet arrived , even though the trajectory is rising toward summer. The trajectory shows up in the gradation.
142#HQ:
143#ZS:**Motivations.** To grow, adapt, and renew , themselves and their context. To stay open despite difficulty. To begin, and begin again. To move toward the world gently but persistently.
144#BT:
145#QN:**How they behave.** Engaged but not loud , present without dominating. They shift with conditions and bounce back easily. They start things , relationships, projects, habits , with genuine hope. They notice small signs of life that others miss.
146#JM:
147#XY:**Strengths.** Resilience and renewal , they recover and restart. Adaptability and openness. Hope that is earned, not naive. Gentleness with real persistence. They draw others out , their openness invites others'.
148#SS:
149#ZJ:**Blind spots.** Over-extending tenderness , staying too long in cold situations. Mistaking adaptability for not having needs. Beginning more than they can sustain. Underestimating their own wattage. Avoiding necessary hardness or conflict.
150#PY:
151#YS:**Growth.** Discern where to grow , not every crack is soil. Claim your needs , adaptability without boundaries burns out. Let some springs become summers , commit and intensify. Practice staying when it is hard, not just starting when it is fresh.
152#HM:
153#MJ:**Relationships.** Spring people offer warmth, openness, and the gift of second chances. They see and nurture others' growth. Risk: pouring into people who do not reciprocate. Growth: be renewed *by* their relationships, not just *for* them.
154#QH:
155#KP:**Work.** They thrive in evolving, mission-driven, people-oriented environments. They shine in roles requiring empathy, adaptation, and renewal , teaching, coaching, care, growth. Risk: under-claiming credit and burning out from giving. Ideal environments value tenderness and tenacity equally.
156#TT:
157#SK:**Decision-making.** Collaborative, values-led, comfortable revising. They decide adaptively and rarely get locked in. Risk: changing course too often and under-committing. Strength: they rarely make rigid, irreversible errors.
158#TV:
159#QP:**Under stress.** The signature is trying harder, giving more, keeping growing through it. They may neglect their own roots while tending others'. Recovery requires returning to their own soil , rest, slowness, fewer outputs. Watch for chronic over-giving read as "just being helpful."
160#ZB:
161#ZW:**Communication.** Warm, encouraging, inclusive, often modest. They make people feel safe to grow. Growth: hold their ground when it matters , soft does not mean small. Their encouragement is catalytic. They should use it on themselves too.

163#QB:**The complementary season.** Autumn. Spring's wholeness lives in discernment , Autumn's capacity to keep what matters and release what does not. Having mastered beginning, the next mastery is choosing what to let end.
